title: TEST - Seka ExAero GR: The Chinese gravel racing bike that's driving everyone crazy

takeaways.text: Repeats SEKA's claims: one-piece monocoque frame of Toray T1100G and M46J at 980 g raw in size 54, a seatstay 'wind eye' that lets the rear flex about 16 mm, 423 mm chainstays, and 56 mm front / 52 mm rear tire clearance (Italian, automatic captions).
FIDLOCK-latched down-tube storage with a supplied bag that opens one-handed, rubber chainstay and down-tube guards, threaded T47, and a mount for 2× as well as 1×.
Sold only as a frame kit (frame, fork, Gladius GR integrated cockpit and seatpost, 15 bar/stem combinations, straight or 15 mm setback post) at €3,099 in March 2026.
The top-spec size-54 test build weighed 7.9 kg without pedals and just over 8 kg with them.

At 172 cm the tester found the 54 compact and racy; it climbs like a road bike and is fastest on flat gravel, but is stiff and demanding on rough descents, so he recommends lower-profile wheels and careful tire pressure for rough terrain.

disclosure: This is a professional publication test; the product-supply and commercial terms were not independently verified.
summary: Italian-language hands-on test covering the ExAero GR platform on varied terrain; treat ride impressions separately from official specifications.
